run.procedureSummary: Step 1 Charge: add the cycle's table row to each crucible, with no capacity limit. Step 2 Overflow: go through positions 1 to 6 in order. Where a crucible holds more than its capacity, cut it to capacity and add the excess to the next crucible before checking that one, so overflow can carry down the line in a single pass. Excess from crucible 6 goes to slag. Step 3 State check, using the post-overflow quantities and each crucible's state from before this check: BASE with quantity >= upper mark becomes SUPERHEATED; SUPERHEATED with quantity <= lower mark becomes BASE; anything else stays as it is. Each crucible changes state at most once per check. Step 4 Draws: work out every draw from the post-state-check quantities first, then apply them all together. BASE draws floor(q/4) to slag. SUPERHEATED draws floor(q/2) to crucible i-1, except crucible 1, which sends it to slag. A crucible left over capacity stays that way until the next cycle's Step 2, or to the end after cycle 5. Step 5 Global reset: if the line total after draws is strictly greater than 38, each crucible keeps floor(q/2) and the rest goes to slag. Simulated with a short Python script (C:\Users\Jaket\AppData\Local\Temp\om\desk-250\cascade.py). I checked cycle 1 and the cycle 2 state changes by hand and they match the script.

openPoints.point: Overflow order: does excess that runs into the next crucible get checked again in the same pass?
openPoints.assumption: Yes. The pass runs 1 to 6 in order, so an overfilled downstream crucible spills on when its turn comes in that same pass (for example, cycle 1 cascaded 2->3->4->5).

openPoints.point: Draw basis: are draws figured on quantities before or after the other draws arrive?
openPoints.assumption: All draws come from the post-state-check quantities and are applied at the same time, as the write-up says ('all figured before moving'). Material that arrives by the return launder is not drawn again in the same step.
The state just set in Step 3 of the same cycle.
'Over 38' means strictly greater than 38. Cycle 5 ended at exactly 38, so no reset fired.

openPoints.point: Reset rounding and where the remainder goes
openPoints.assumption: Each crucible keeps floor(q/2). Everything removed, including odd units, goes to slag.
A crucible that just went BASE to SUPERHEATED is not tested against the lower mark in the same check, and the reverse also holds.
The loss tally is the slag tally: overflow from crucible 6, BASE draws, crucible 1's SUPERHEATED draws, and reset removals.

run.balanceCheck: Starting melt 20 + charges 94 (15+17+17+24+18... per cycle: 20, 15, 17, 24, 18) = 114; end melt 38 (6+10+9+7+4+2) + slag 76 = 114. Balanced.
